nodes.label: AMPM Platform Test Cases Mapped to Acceptance Criteria (DRAFT v0.2, 25 Oct 2026)
nodes.rationale: Extends SPEC section 12 (fifteen acceptance scenarios) and section 14 (test cases mapped to acceptance criteria): every criterion has at least one test, every test cites the flow and screens it exercises, and the traceability matrix is the index. AMPM's decisions of 25 October 2026 are applied where they change a test and stamped on every assumption.

nodes.label: requirements-audit.md (Q numbers)
data-model.md (A-1 to A-30)
permission-matrix.md (P-1 to P-11, transitions, automation, audited actions)
field-matrix.md (validations)
architecture.md (T-1 to T-14, enforcement, delivery)
user-flows.md (Flow 1 to 12, U-1 to U-12)
wireframes.md (screen IDs, W-1 to W-15)
SPEC (AMPM platform specification: sections 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14)
nodes.rationale: The specification is the source of truth being extended; SPEC section 12 gives AC-01 to AC-15 and sections 10, 7, 8, 9 imply AC-16 to AC-36.

nodes.label: Assumptions register V-1 to V-16 (verification-specific)
nodes.rationale: Verification-specific assumptions are kept separate from data-model (A), permission (P), technology (T), flow (U) and wireframe (W) assumptions, each stamped with AMPM's 25 October 2026 decision and an 'if AMPM decides otherwise' consequence.

nodes.label: Changes from AMPM's decisions (25 October 2026), section 0a
AMPM's acceptance checklist (20 scenarios) mapped to tests
Test case format AC-nn.m (type and priority, principal, preconditions, steps, expected, references)
Test levels and tooling (architecture section 4 row 20, section 12)
Unit tests (Vitest, every pull request)
API integration tests (Supertest against disposable PostgreSQL and Redis, every pull request)
Generated authorisation and transition suite (from the permission matrix CSV)
nodes.rationale: Generated from permission-matrix sections 5, 6 and 7 so a change in the matrix changes the tests without hand editing; fails the build on drift (V-16). A code change that widens access without a matrix change fails too.

nodes.label: Generated validation suite (field-matrix.csv rules to API tests)
nodes.rationale: Every field with a validation rule in the field matrix gets a violating and a valid request; the suite fails the build when a field has no test.

nodes.label: End-to-end tests (Playwright against staging with the synthetic seed)
nodes.rationale: Each flow in user-flows.md becomes one Playwright journey; the acceptance tests are its assertions. Runs on every merge to main; full pack before a phase exit.

nodes.label: Contract tests (adapter tests against provider sandboxes, nightly and before release)
Load and performance tests (k6 profiles, before each phase exit)
Accessibility tests (axe-core in Playwright plus manual screen-reader passes)
Security tests (dependency and image scanning, ZAP baseline nightly, Phase 5 penetration test)
Infrastructure tests (Terraform plan checks, compliance rules, restore drill)
Test priorities P1, P2, P3
nodes.rationale: P1 blocks the phase exit and any release; P2 must pass before the phase exit but may be waived for an interim release with a recorded reason; P3 is tracked and fixed before launch.

nodes.label: Principals used in tests (SA, SM, HT, PM, CD, VC, RG, HL, FA; CO, CA, CV; GU; DP; SYS; '(a)' member, '(other)' non-member)
Denial semantics: 404 for invisible records, 403 for forbidden actions, 400 for validation, 409 for transition guards
nodes.rationale: A principal that may not see a record receives 404 with the same body as for a nonexistent record so existence cannot be inferred; a visible record with a forbidden action gets 403; validation failures return 400 naming the field; status-transition violations return 409 with the guard message. Tests assert these codes exactly.

nodes.label: Environments and data: synthetic seed, explicitly triggered jobs, injectable clocks
nodes.rationale: Jobs are triggered explicitly in tests rather than waited for, and clocks are injectable so expiry, reminder and retention behaviour can be tested without waiting (V-6).

nodes.label: Traceability matrix (criterion, source, tests, flows, screens, phase)
Phase exit packs (SPEC section 11; scope per V-11)
Phase 1 Foundation exit pack: lead-to-subscriber journey tested; private data protected
Phase 2 Wedding planning exit pack: a sample wedding planned and approved end to end
Phase 3 Guest operations exit pack: guest data flows into operational reports
Phase 4 Live execution exit pack: a simulated event managed through closure
Phase 5 Stabilisation exit pack: critical defects resolved; launch checklist signed
Non-functional test plan (availability 99.5%, p95 under 400 ms, interactive under 3 s on 4G, WCAG 2.1 AA, RPO 15 min / RTO 4 h, twice A-15 capacity)
nodes.rationale: Load profiles use synthetic data at V-5 volumes against staging with provider sandboxes; production is never load tested.

nodes.label: Synthetic seed and fixtures (one idempotent load shared by every suite, versioned with the code)
nodes.rationale: No fixture contains real names, numbers, addresses or images (V-15); every suite starts from a clean load.

nodes.label: Sample wedding AMPM-2027-014 (four functions, 168 households, 412 guests, checklists in every state)
Automation strategy (generators, pull request gate, staging deploy, phase exit pack, tagged release)
nodes.rationale: Two generated suites keep the documents and the code honest; release gating follows architecture section 12 with no production deploy while any wedding is live (T-14).

nodes.label: Coverage summary (38 criteria, 220 test identifiers) and open questions for the test review
Idempotency of jobs, webhooks and submissions
nodes.rationale: Repeated job runs, duplicate webhook deliveries and double submissions must produce one effect: idempotency key provider_ref for payments, idempotency keys on form submissions, and 'second run changes nothing' assertions on freshness, recalculation and escalation jobs.

nodes.label: Schema assertion over client-facing responses (additional properties forbidden)
nodes.rationale: Finance-leak and restricted-field tests compare every client-facing response against the serialiser schema rather than spot checks (V-8); sentinel values are seeded into every restricted, sensitive, secret and bank field and must never appear in any CO, CA, CV, GU or DP body.

nodes.label: V-1 Payment tests use the gateway sandbox, test keys, simulated webhooks and the manual bank-transfer path
nodes.rationale: No real card or bank data is ever used. AMPM 2026-10-25: partly decided; the gateway sandbox depends on the provider choice. Offline-only payments would deactivate the gateway tests.

nodes.label: V-2 Messaging tests use provider sandboxes; WhatsApp templates stubbed until approved; delivery webhooks simulated
nodes.rationale: AMPM 2026-10-25: partly decided; sandboxes depend on the provider choice. Dropping a channel removes its tests.

nodes.label: V-3 Authentication tests: email and password, authenticator codes for staff, OTP for clients and prospects, guest token links; no registration test
nodes.rationale: There is no registration test because there is no registration. AMPM 2026-10-25: changed to OTP sign-in tests for clients and prospects (AC-17.9).

nodes.label: V-4 Offline tests run in the first release on native builds (was Phase 4 browser offline emulation)
nodes.rationale: AMPM 2026-10-25: changed; native apps with offline use at launch move AC-33, AC-13.5 and AC-14.5 to the first release on native builds. Without offline support those tests are removed.

nodes.label: V-5 Load tests run at twice the sizing assumptions (rescaled to 200 hotels, 20 weddings; staff and guest numbers to confirm)
nodes.rationale: Originally 100 concurrent staff, 1,500 guests in one hour, 500 hotels with T-12 targets. AMPM 2026-10-25: changed; profiles rescaled, numbers to be confirmed.

nodes.label: V-6 Retention tests use accelerated clocks (periods set to minutes) and cover the approval workflow, not automatic deletion
nodes.rationale: Retention periods are configuration, so periods change the configuration, not the tests. AMPM 2026-10-25: changed; the retention job proposes and nothing is deleted until SA approves.

nodes.label: V-7 Identity-document tests use synthetic images and a fictitious Aadhaar-format number to prove rejection
nodes.rationale: No real identity document ever enters a test environment. AMPM 2026-10-25: confirmed.

nodes.label: V-8 Finance-leak tests assert the absence of internal fields by schema comparison across screens, exports, notifications and APIs
nodes.rationale: Schema comparison, not spot checks. AMPM 2026-10-25: confirmed. A transparent fee model keeps the tests because the internal fields still exist.

nodes.label: V-9 RSVP tests: per-side link tests activate; household-token tests become the alternative
nodes.rationale: Originally one token per household with a dormant open-link set. AMPM 2026-10-25: changed; the per-side link tests AC-10.11 to AC-10.13 are activated.

nodes.label: V-10 Demo isolation tests assume demo data in the same database behind flags and prove no query path reaches non-demo rows
nodes.rationale: AMPM 2026-10-25: partly decided; demo content changed, isolation tests stand. A separate demo database would replace these with an environment-separation check.

nodes.label: V-11 Phase exit packs follow the first-release scope
nodes.rationale: Originally the Phase 1 scope of A-10 (demo, full consultancy statuses, online payment, built-in CMS). AMPM 2026-10-25: changed; items leaving Phase 1 move their tests to the later phase's pack.

nodes.label: V-12 GST invoice tests dropped: no GST invoices from the platform
nodes.rationale: AMPM 2026-10-25: dropped. AC-36.3 and AC-36.4 are dormant; invoices come from an accounting system.

nodes.label: V-13 Backup and restore drills run quarterly in staging; first drill is a Phase 5 exit gate; RPO and RTO measured, not assumed
nodes.rationale: AMPM 2026-10-25: still open; recovery targets to be confirmed. Tighter targets change the thresholds.

nodes.label: V-14 On-behalf decision tests require an evidence document and assert the audit badge
nodes.rationale: AMPM 2026-10-25: confirmed. Forbidding on-behalf decisions would turn those tests into denial tests.

nodes.label: V-15 Test data is synthetic; staging never holds real guest data
nodes.rationale: Fictitious names, phone numbers in reserved ranges, example-domain emails, generated images (architecture section 12). Not addressed by AMPM; stands.

nodes.label: V-16 The authorisation suite is generated from permission-matrix sections 5 and 6
nodes.rationale: A change in the matrix changes the tests without hand editing. Not addressed by AMPM; stands.

nodes.label: Q1 Native apps with offline use at launch
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: offline tests move to the first release on native builds; AC-33.5 and AC-33.6 added.

nodes.label: Q2 Payment gateway and online payment
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: partly decided; the gateway sandbox used by the payment tests depends on the provider choice.

nodes.label: Q3 Demo serves as the trial; renewal restores data
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: renewal restores access and preserves data (AC-02.11); the trial test AC-02.8 is dormant because the demo serves as the trial.

nodes.label: Q4 Milestone payments not online in the first release; internal costs never shown to clients
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: any test paying a milestone online (CP-25) is dormant; AC-28.1 covers subscription payments only.

nodes.label: Q5 On-behalf decisions by staff with evidence
Q6 Department-based access
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: new criterion AC-38; which roles see cost fields is still to be finalised.

nodes.label: Q7 RSVP links per side or combined; no guest editing after submission
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: AC-10.11 to AC-10.13 activated as the per-side tests; AC-10.3 (guest edits) becomes a denial test; AC-10.1 identifies the household on a side link.

nodes.label: Q8 Identity documents: synthetic test data, no automatic deletion
Q10 Only Eva's authorised personnel (SA) approve readiness and closure exceptions
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: in AC-13.2 and AC-15.6 the Project Manager's authorisation attempt must return 403; only SA succeeds.

nodes.label: Q11 Messaging providers (WhatsApp, SMS, email)
Q12 No website editing (no CMS) in the current release
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: no CMS tests remain active; AC-25.1 covers reference data only; the generated route inventory in AC-02.10 proves no CMS route exists.

nodes.label: Q13 Mobile OTP sign-in for prospects and clients
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: new test AC-17.9; AC-17.2 becomes the OTP path for every client sign-in; AC-17.6 applies to staff only.

nodes.label: Q14 Backup and recovery targets
Q15 Sizing: about 200 hotels and 20 weddings
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: AC-34 profiles rescaled to 200 hotels, 40 concurrent staff, 20 weddings; guest numbers to confirm.

nodes.label: Q16 No GST invoices issued from the platform
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: AC-36.3 and AC-36.4 are dormant.

nodes.label: Q17 Retention: no automatic deletion; synthetic test data
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: AC-15.8 and AC-27.3 become approval-workflow tests; the retention job proposes and nothing is deleted until SA approves.

nodes.label: Q20 Live chat alongside tracked requests
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-10-25: new criterion AC-37.

nodes.label: AC-01 Public enquiry saves source and owner; team tracks follow-up
nodes.rationale: Duplicate leads are flagged, never refused or auto-merged; a converted lead becomes read-only and the only path to an account is an invitation.

nodes.label: AC-02 Subscription activates hotel discovery without exposing full wedding modules
nodes.rationale: Online purchase, manual bank transfer and renewal all activate exactly the plan's modules; expiry removes modules and nothing else; the trial test AC-02.8 is dormant because the demo serves as the trial (Q3); no self-registration route exists.

nodes.label: AC-03 Demo account cannot access records outside demo scope
nodes.rationale: Demo data lives in the same database behind flags (V-10); rates are masked, non-demo hotels are 404, demo rows are invisible to operational staff and demo users cannot export.

nodes.label: AC-04 Hotel search shows freshness of pricing; unverified availability is never shown as confirmed
nodes.rationale: Verified, stale and unverified cards carry distinct labels; the word 'confirmed' must not appear in rate context; availability is labelled separately from rates and answered inside an enquiry.

nodes.label: AC-05 AMPM records negotiation and site visit without exposing internal notes
nodes.rationale: Internal-only events, restricted enquiry fields and hotel contacts never serialise to clients; 'preview as client' must be byte-identical to the real client response; an enquiry is not a confirmed booking until a done confirmed milestone and a signed contract exist; chargeable services wait for an active agreement.

nodes.label: AC-06 Engaged client receives correct project and permissions
nodes.rationale: Project creation needs only minimal fields and back-fills saved hotels, enquiry and agreement; client roles and the finance flag shape the portal with no placeholder for missing regions; membership removal ends access immediately; on-behalf decisions need evidence and a badge (V-14).

nodes.label: AC-07 Multiple functions have independent vendors, schedules, budgets and approvals
nodes.rationale: Approving one function's proposal leaves the other untouched; cancelling a function keeps its records (soft delete).

nodes.label: AC-08 Vendor shortlist permits fewer than five options; it does not require exactly ten
nodes.rationale: SPEC 1.2 says 'aiming for 5 to 10' but two options and twelve options must both present cleanly; availability conflicts warn but do not block.

nodes.label: AC-09 Approval refers to the exact design, menu or proposal version; revisions do not overwrite it
nodes.rationale: A new version supersedes and the old one is immutable; approval locks the version and budget line; menu approval freezes the guaranteed headcount; approving an invitation does not send it.

nodes.label: AC-10 Self-service and AMPM-assisted RSVP update the same guest database without duplicates
nodes.rationale: Both paths upsert the same guest_function_attendance rows and add rsvp_responses snapshots; per-side links identify the household (Q7); submitted responses are locked and corrections go through the RSVP team; allergies are sensitive; identity capture is conditional and audited.

nodes.label: AC-11 Attendance changes update totals and flag downstream planning impacts
nodes.rationale: Recalculation changes expected_count but never guaranteed_count; rooming and transfer changes are flagged and logistics notified once; recalculation is idempotent.

nodes.label: AC-12 Unauthorised users cannot access restricted data by changing URLs, API requests or file links
nodes.rationale: A generated suite covers every resource, principal and action; identifier tampering returns 404 with bodies and timing identical to a nonexistent id; signed file links expire and bind to one file; break-glass reads by SA are audited and alerted.

nodes.label: AC-13 Production readiness cannot be completed without required checks or an authorised exception
nodes.rationale: Readiness derives automatically from required items; exceptions may only be authorised by SA (Q10), PM and HL attempts return 403.

nodes.label: AC-14 Incidents can be assigned, escalated and closed with resolution notes
nodes.rationale: Critical incidents escalate automatically along the configured chain; critical resolution requires notes; client visibility is off by default and never exposes description or notes.

nodes.label: AC-15 Closure checks departure, lost-and-found, vendor completion and financial reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Each closure item verifies against data (409 until satisfied); closing deletes nothing; client access ends after the configured window and only SA may reopen; retention after closure requires SA approval (Q17).

nodes.label: AC-16 Responsive and accessible interfaces
nodes.rationale: Key screens render at 1280, 1024 and 375 px; WCAG 2.1 AA via axe-core; the guest wizard gets a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass.

nodes.label: AC-17 Secure authentication
nodes.rationale: Staff must enrol an authenticator before first use; clients and prospects sign in by mobile OTP (Q13); lockout with generic errors; single-use time-boxed tokens; Argon2id password storage; guest sessions bound to the household token.

nodes.label: AC-18 Server-side validation on every protected request
nodes.rationale: Validations are generated from field-matrix.csv; required-at-stage rules return 409; mass assignment of internal_cost, is_demo or status is never applied; uniqueness returns 409.

nodes.label: AC-19 Encryption in transit and at rest
nodes.rationale: TLS 1.2+ with HSTS; three customer-managed keys with the restricted bucket on its own key; no secrets in code, images or logs.

nodes.label: AC-20 Private file storage, expiring links and safe uploads
nodes.rationale: Content-type detection, size limits, antivirus scan, image metadata stripping; document access follows the owning record's visibility.

nodes.label: AC-21 Audit trail
nodes.rationale: Every listed action writes one event with actor, entity, before and after; audit_events is append-only at the database level and partitioned monthly; viewer scope follows roles.

nodes.label: AC-22 Backups and tested restoration
nodes.rationale: Point-in-time restore drill within 4 hours and 15 minutes of data (RPO/RTO measured, not assumed, V-13); object storage restore from versions and replica region; backup failure alerts.

nodes.label: AC-23 Search, filters, pagination and bulk operations
nodes.rationale: Keyset pagination at 50 per page with no duplicates or gaps; bulk operations run as one job with one audit event per changed row; trigram hotel search relevance.

nodes.label: AC-24 Media optimisation and controlled video delivery
nodes.rationale: Derivatives generated by job; video transcoded and served only with expiring signed tokens; rights status gates client and public visibility.

nodes.label: AC-25 Configurable packages, categories, statuses and pricing
nodes.rationale: Reference data edits take effect without a deploy; thresholds drive automation; a CI static check fails the build on any commercial literal in code (BIZ rule 8).

nodes.label: AC-26 Clear errors, duplicate-submission prevention and form recovery
nodes.rationale: Double submission creates one record via idempotency keys; drafts survive refresh; errors name the field, keep input and are announced to assistive technology.

nodes.label: AC-27 Retention, deletion and privacy
nodes.rationale: Consent is captured with its notice version; data principal export and erasure anonymise personal fields but keep attendance counts; retention deletes only after SA approval; logs contain no personal data.

nodes.label: AC-28 Integration boundaries
nodes.rationale: Adapters are contract-tested against sandboxes; card data never leaves AMPM; provider outages retry with backoff and dead-letter; payloads carry only the fields listed in architecture section 10.

nodes.label: AC-29 Notifications and automation
nodes.rationale: Approval requests go to CO and approvers with can_approve, never CV; material changes create review tasks; the notification log is complete; preferences and opt-in are honoured.

nodes.label: AC-30 Reports and exports
nodes.rationale: Every SPEC section 9 report computes from the seed; permissions follow permission-matrix section 5.16; the rooming list export for hotels carries names, dates and room category only.

nodes.label: AC-31 Status transitions and guards
nodes.rationale: Transition tests are generated from permission-matrix section 7: unlisted principals get 403, unlisted transitions get 409 with the guard message; status labels are display only.

nodes.label: AC-32 Entitlement resolution and downgrades
nodes.rationale: Each account state yields exactly the documented module set; downgrade is read-only before removal; the entitlement cache is invalidated on write, not only on expiry.

nodes.label: AC-33 Offline behaviour on event day
nodes.rationale: Read caches with an 'offline since' indicator; queued mutations sync in order with original timestamps; server status wins conflicts and the offline change is logged; local data is encrypted and wiped on sign-out (first release on native builds, Q1).

nodes.label: AC-34 Performance and capacity
nodes.rationale: k6 profiles for hotel search, RSVP burst, team workspace mixed load and job throughput; profiles rescaled to 200 hotels and 20 weddings (Q15).

nodes.label: AC-35 Imports
nodes.rationale: Hotel and guest imports validate first and apply with audit per row; duplicates by phone are flagged, not merged; identity columns are refused, allergies only through the sensitive mapping step.

nodes.label: AC-36 Finance integrity
nodes.rationale: Client and internal amounts never mix (schema assertion); approved amounts are locked except for an audited FA override; GST invoice tests AC-36.3 and AC-36.4 are dormant (Q16); refunds cannot exceed the original payment.

nodes.label: AC-37 Live chat alongside tracked requests
nodes.rationale: Conversations reach staff within two seconds and can become tracked client_requests; chat never carries an approval; conversations are isolated per account; unanswered conversations surface to the department lead (Q20).

nodes.label: AC-38 Department-based access
nodes.rationale: Each department sees only the resources permission-matrix section 5 grants; project membership bounds every department; cost visibility is limited to roles AMPM still has to finalise (Q6).

nodes.label: AC-02.11 Renewal restores access and preserves data
nodes.rationale: Nothing is deleted on expiry, so a new subscription makes the six saved hotels and both enquiries reachable again with their history (Q3).

nodes.label: AC-10.11 Side link: a guest identifies their household
nodes.rationale: An exact match opens the household's RSVP; a near match is held for RSVP-team review; no household data is shown before a confirmed match; a groom-side household cannot be found through the bride-side link (Q7).

nodes.label: AC-10.12 Unmatched guests are held for review
nodes.rationale: A pending household with identification_status review counts for nothing until the RSVP team approves (Q7).

nodes.label: AC-10.13 Submitted responses are locked; corrections go through the team
nodes.rationale: The reopened link shows a read-only summary; a correction request creates a guest_support_requests row and RG's change writes the same attendance rows with response_source ampm_call (Q7).

nodes.label: AC-17.9 Mobile OTP sign-in for prospects and clients
nodes.rationale: Codes are single use and expire in ten minutes; an uninvited number receives a neutral message and no session (Q13).

nodes.label: AC-33.5 Local data is protected on native builds
nodes.rationale: The local store is encrypted at rest, holds only the user's role-scoped data and is wiped on sign-out (Q1).

nodes.label: AC-33.6 Offline state and pending changes are visible
nodes.rationale: An offline banner shows the pending-change count, which drains to zero on reconnect with each change keeping its original time (Q1).

hyperedges.label: Criteria whose P1 and P2 tests gate the Phase 1 Foundation exit
Suites generated from the permission matrix and field matrix that fail the build on drift
Client-facing responses never carry internal costs, margins, private rates, contacts or sensitive guest fields
